stem:
A physically opioid-dependent patient takes standard-dose sublingual buprenorphine soon after using heroin, before spontaneous withdrawal begins. Soon afterwards, abdominal cramps, sweating and agitation abruptly worsen.

Which mechanism best explains the deterioration?

options.label: A
options.text: Inhibition of opioid breakdown in the liver
options.explanation: This is a receptor-occupancy effect, not accumulation caused by inhibited hepatic breakdown.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Muscarinic activation does not explain the timing after a high-affinity opioid medication.

options.label: C
options.text: Blockade of renal elimination of heroin
options.explanation: Renal elimination does not explain the abrupt reduction in opioid effect and withdrawal symptoms.

options.label: D
options.text: Increased full agonist activity at opioid receptors
options.explanation: Buprenorphine provides less intrinsic receptor activation than a full agonist, so replacing heroin can reduce rather than increase net activity.

options.label: E
options.text: Displacement by a high-affinity partial agonist
options.explanation: Buprenorphine can displace a full agonist while providing less opioid effect, precipitating withdrawal if standard induction begins too early.

context: High receptor affinity plus partial agonism explains buprenorphine-precipitated withdrawal.
